classification: derived arithmetic and revised interpretation; no forecast values changed
user_intervention: Challenge whether we actually reject management volume recovery and whether macro weakness explains continuing non-Jeep performance.
correction: Previous emphasis on ex-Ram-LD decline was accurate but incomplete: it hid the concentration of weakness in Jeep and could imply generalized non-Ram demand failure. The numerical forecast is not a demonstrated management haircut.

management.scope: North American American brands, customer sales, 2025–2030
management.industry_assumption: flat industry through 2030; growth from share/segment expansion

research_forecast.scope: 13 US families, customer sales, 2025–2028; not full future product portfolio
research_forecast.comparison_limit: Different geography, family/brand coverage and end-year. Similar annualized rates show no established bearish haircut, but do not prove matched forecasts agree.

macro.observed: Industry sales pace +3.3% MoM; inventory down YoY. Vehicles <=30k:54days supply; >60k:over90. Affordability pressure and healthy aggregate demand coexist.
macro.inference: Post-shortage supply restoration does not by itself restore attractive consumer payments or competitive positioning. No evidence here establishes a broad current macro contraction causing all STLA brands to decline.
macro.limitation: Price-band stock-to-sales differences do not estimate demand elasticity; no matched financing/price/retail panel.

revised_position: Buy the plausibility of selective recovery and broader affordable offerings. Unresolved issues are launch timing, external customer conquest versus own-lineup substitution, competitive pricing and retained profit. Absence of mature launch evidence is uncertainty, not proof of failure. Current weak level versus historic peaks is distinct from current growth rate.
